assumptionReview.assumption: ANSI escape regex coverage scope: cover CSI sequences only (`\x1B[` + parameter bytes + intermediate bytes + final byte). DCS / OSC / single-shifts out of scope for v1; bare ESC byte caught by C0 regex.
assumptionReview.rationale: Verified at src/internal/format-error-embed.ts:43 — pattern `/\x1B\[[0-9;?]*[ -/]*[@-~]/g` covers CSI per the assumption text. The CSI form is the dominant log-injection vector (color/cursor manipulation in terminal viewers); DCS/OSC/single-shifts are rarely used adversarially and would be out of scope for a v1 sanitizer per spec/review-security.md. Bare ESC byte is caught by the C0 regex pass at line 51 (C0 includes 0x1B). The redaction is defense-in-depth — the C0 fallback ensures any escape byte that snuck past the CSI regex still gets redacted. Pattern is character-class only with no nested quantifiers — no backtracking risk. ACCEPTABLE.

assumptionReview.assumption: Truncation order in formatErrorEmbed: redact FIRST, JSON.stringify SECOND, truncate LAST. Truncation operates on JSON-stringified length (the `"..."` quote pair counts toward the 120-char limit).
assumptionReview.rationale: Verified at src/internal/format-error-embed.ts:102-121. Step ordering is exactly as documented (line 107 redact, line 110 JSON.stringify, lines 117-118 truncate). The alternative (JSON.stringify FIRST then redact) would convert `\x07` to the JSON-escaped `\u0007` and the C0 regex would never match — the redaction token would never appear. Verified empirically by the T-077 control-char redaction tests at format-error-embed.test.ts:39-72 — all pass. Truncating the JSON-stringified form is the right choice — the visible rendered length matches the user-visible embed (the `"..."` quotes are part of what operators see). Boundary semantics correct: a 118-char input → 120-char output (passes through; line 118 vs ellipsis); a 119-char input → 121-char output (truncates with ellipsis at line 121). ACCEPTABLE.

The generator's reasoning that the cap-first ordering is also benign because slice(0, 255) is left-anchored is correct, but cap-LAST is structurally cleaner because it eliminates the case-by-case argument.
